title: Xi Pledges China Will Lead AI, Tech Cooperation Push for BRICS
excerpt: At the BRICS leaders' summit in New Delhi, China's president unveiled a 'Greater BRICS Initiative' including a BRICS AI Open Source Zone, a special economic zone partnership and a service trade forum.
body:
• Chinese President Xi Jinping said China will take the lead in establishing a BRICS AI Open Source Zone covering large language models, AI training and an open AI ecosystem.
  • Xi unveiled the plan on Sunday at the BRICS leaders' summit in New Delhi as part of a "Greater BRICS Initiative" spanning AI, trade and industrial cooperation.
  • He also proposed a BRICS Special Economic Zone partnership and said China would host a BRICS Service Trade Forum next year to boost trade and investment ties.
  • The push comes with India holding the 2026 BRICS chair and China set to take over in 2027, as the expanded bloc seeks a larger global role.

Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday positioned China as the driving force behind a new wave of technology cooperation among BRICS nations, announcing that Beijing will take the lead in establishing a BRICS AI Open Source Zone at the bloc's leaders' summit in New Delhi.

Xi unveiled a package of initiatives ranging from artificial intelligence to trade under what he called the "Greater BRICS Initiative," aimed at welding the expanded grouping into a practical platform for Global South development, according to the official Xinhua news agency. Addressing the summit's closing session, he said "Greater BRICS" nations should cooperate more closely, maintain the stability of industrial and supply chains, and cultivate an integrated market.

Context & Background

The BRICS bloc has grown well beyond its original five members — Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Iran, Indonesia, Egypt, Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates have since joined the grouping, and 10 partner countries now extend its reach across Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Middle East. China and Russia sometimes refer to this larger formation as "Greater BRICS." India holds the bloc's rotating chair in 2026, with China set to take over in 2027.

Xi's technology pitch builds on a campaign he has waged all year. At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai in July, he argued that AI development should be a global effort rather than the preserve of any single nation, pushed back against what he called the "overstretching" of national security concerns in AI, and promised 5,000 AI training opportunities for developing countries over five years — plus access for 30 countries to a Chinese-built AI meteorological early-warning system. Days earlier, Beijing had launched the China-created World AI Cooperation Organisation, which signed up 29 member countries.

"The development of artificial intelligence should not be a solo performance by any single country but rather a symphony of global cooperation."

— Xi Jinping, President of China, at the World AI Conference in Shanghai, July 2026

Impact & Analysis

The AI Open Source Zone is the centerpiece: a Chinese-led framework for cooperation on large language models, AI training and an open AI ecosystem across BRICS economies. It fits Beijing's broader pitch of low-cost, open-source AI models as a tool for narrowing global disparities in AI access — a direct contrast with U.S.-led restrictions that have blocked China from some of the world's most advanced technologies and spurred its drive to build domestic know-how.

The economic proposals carry weight too. A Special Economic Zone partnership and a BRICS Service Trade Forum hosted by China next year signal Beijing's intent to bind the bloc together with trade and investment ties, not just summit communiques. Xi himself told the summit that the success of the "Greater BRICS Initiative" depends on laying a solid foundation for pragmatic cooperation, according to Xinhua.

What's Next

China will host the BRICS Service Trade Forum next year and takes the bloc's chair in 2027, giving Beijing two platforms to advance the AI and trade agenda. The test will be whether the Open Source Zone and the economic-zone partnership move from summit pledges to funded programs — and how Washington responds to a rival AI ecosystem taking shape across the Global South.
